questions.q: The workers would rather ____ overtime than lose their jobs.
questions.x: Correct answer: do. 'Would rather' takes a bare infinitive.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
If I (would have known) about the inspection, I would have kept the registers ready.
questions.x: Correct answer: had known. Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
No sooner had the minister arrived / than the protesters / began shouting slogans.
o: No sooner had the minister arrived
questions.x: The sentence is grammatically correct as written. The sentence is correct.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
The report, along with its annexures, (were sent) to the Ministry on Monday.
questions.x: Correct answer: was sent. The subject is 'the report'; 'along with' does not make it plural.

questions.q: We have ____ printing paper; please place an order immediately.
questions.x: 'Run out of' means have no more left.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to 'candid' as used in: 'The officer was known for her candid remarks about the scheme's failures.'
questions.x: Candid means frank; its opposite is evasive.

questions.q:
Rearrange the following sentences (P, Q, R, S) to form a coherent paragraph:
P: As a result, many families slip back into poverty after a single hospital stay.
Q: Out-of-pocket spending on health remains high in India.
R: Health insurance schemes aim to break this cycle.
S: Most of this spending goes on medicines and diagnostic tests.
questions.x: Q introduces the problem, S explains it, P gives the consequence and R the remedy.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive form: 'The manager has approved my leave.'
o: My leave was approved by the manager.
My leave has been approved by the manager.
My leave had been approved by the manager.
My leave is approved by the manager.
questions.x: Correct answer: My leave has been approved by the manager.. Present perfect passive: has been + past participle.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The price of pulses / in the local market / have gone up this month.
questions.x: The error is in part (c): 'have gone up this month'. The subject 'the price' is singular: 'has gone up'.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The officer refused to pass the buck and accepted the blame', 'pass the buck' means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Shift responsibility to someone else. To pass the buck is to shift responsibility.

questions.q: The situation described in the first part of the passage is best described as:
o: A problem caused by a single dishonest farmer
A problem of shared resources in which individual gains create collective loss
A shortage created by excessive rainfall
questions.x: Answer: 'A problem of shared resources in which individual gains create collective loss'. No one is to blame individually, but together they empty the aquifer. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: When a resource belongs to everyone, each user has a reason to take a little more before others do. Groundwater is a striking case. A farmer who deepens a borewell gains water for a season, but the falling water table raises costs for every neighbour, who in turn drills deeper. No single farmer is to blame, yet together they empty the aquifer. Villages that have reversed this trend did not rely on outside policing alone; they measured their water, shared the data openly, and agreed on crop choices that the aquifer could sustain.

questions.q: According to the passage, villages that succeeded in protecting groundwater:
o: Measured water, shared data and agreed on suitable crops
questions.x: Answer: 'Measured water, shared data and agreed on suitable crops'. This is stated in the last sentence. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: When a resource belongs to everyone, each user has a reason to take a little more before others do. Groundwater is a striking case. A farmer who deepens a borewell gains water for a season, but the falling water table raises costs for every neighbour, who in turn drills deeper. No single farmer is to blame, yet together they empty the aquifer. Villages that have reversed this trend did not rely on outside policing alone; they measured their water, shared the data openly, and agreed on crop choices that the aquifer could sustain.

questions.q: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
o: Information shared among users can help them manage a common resource
Crop choices have no effect on water use
Groundwater is the private property of each farmer
Deeper borewells solve the water problem permanently
questions.x: Answer: 'Information shared among users can help them manage a common resource'. Openly shared data was part of the successful villages' approach. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: When a resource belongs to everyone, each user has a reason to take a little more before others do. Groundwater is a striking case. A farmer who deepens a borewell gains water for a season, but the falling water table raises costs for every neighbour, who in turn drills deeper. No single farmer is to blame, yet together they empty the aquifer. Villages that have reversed this trend did not rely on outside policing alone; they measured their water, shared the data openly, and agreed on crop choices that the aquifer could sustain.

questions.q: Why, according to the passage, is preventive care undervalued?
o: It is more expensive than surgery
Its successes are invisible because the illness never occurs
questions.x: Answer: 'Its successes are invisible because the illness never occurs'. 'No one celebrates the heart attack that did not happen.' The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Health systems are usually judged by their hospitals, yet the most effective health care often happens far from them. A trained community worker who checks blood pressure, counsels a mother on nutrition or ensures that a child completes vaccination may prevent more suffering than a specialist surgeon. Prevention is undervalued partly because its successes are invisible: no one celebrates the heart attack that did not happen. Budgets, however, should follow outcomes, not visibility.

questions.q: The final sentence of the passage recommends that:
o: Hospitals should receive all health spending
Spending should be guided by health results achieved
Budgets should depend on public popularity
questions.x: Answer: 'Spending should be guided by health results achieved'. 'Budgets … should follow outcomes, not visibility.' The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Health systems are usually judged by their hospitals, yet the most effective health care often happens far from them. A trained community worker who checks blood pressure, counsels a mother on nutrition or ensures that a child completes vaccination may prevent more suffering than a specialist surgeon. Prevention is undervalued partly because its successes are invisible: no one celebrates the heart attack that did not happen. Budgets, however, should follow outcomes, not visibility.

questions.q: Which of the following would the author most likely agree with?
o: Prevention cannot be measured in any way
Vaccination is the responsibility of hospitals alone
A strong network of community health workers can reduce the burden on hospitals
Surgeons are unnecessary in a health system
questions.x: Answer: 'A strong network of community health workers can reduce the burden on hospitals'. Community workers 'may prevent more suffering'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Health systems are usually judged by their hospitals, yet the most effective health care often happens far from them. A trained community worker who checks blood pressure, counsels a mother on nutrition or ensures that a child completes vaccination may prevent more suffering than a specialist surgeon. Prevention is undervalued partly because its successes are invisible: no one celebrates the heart attack that did not happen. Budgets, however, should follow outcomes, not visibility.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Mahayana Buddhism:
1. It emphasises the ideal of the Bodhisattva.
2. It permitted image worship of the Buddha.
3. Its canonical texts were written only in Pali.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Mahayana texts were largely in Sanskrit; the Theravada canon is in Pali.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Theosophical Society:
1. It was founded in New York in 1875 by Madame Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott.
2. Its headquarters later moved to Adyar near Madras.
3. It was founded by Annie Besant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Annie Besant joined later and led the Society in India.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Tribal revolts in the 19th century were often directed at outsiders ('dikus').
Reason (R): Colonial land and forest laws enabled moneylenders, traders and contractors to dispossess tribal communities.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Indian classical music:
1. Purandara Dasa is called the father of Carnatic music.
2. Khayal is a form of Hindustani music.
3. Thyagaraja composed mainly in Persian.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Thyagaraja composed mostly in Telugu.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Hindustani and Carnatic music:
1. Both are based on the concepts of raga and tala.
2. Purandara Dasa is regarded as the father of Carnatic music.
3. Thyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri are called the 'Trinity' of Hindustani music.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
They are the Trinity of Carnatic music.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924–25):
1. It demanded that lower castes be allowed to use roads near the Vaikom temple in Travancore.
2. E. V. Ramasamy (Periyar) took part in it.
3. It was led by B. R. Ambedkar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Leaders included T. K. Madhavan and K. P. Kesava Menon.

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. Rowlatt Satyagraha 2. Champaran Satyagraha 3. Kheda Satyagraha 4. Non-Cooperation Movement
questions.x: Champaran (1917), Kheda (1918), Rowlatt (1919), Non-Cooperation (1920).

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Dadabhai Naoroji argued that British rule caused a 'drain of wealth' from India.
Reason (R): Home charges, such as pensions and salaries of British officials and interest on debt, were paid out of Indian revenues.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Naoroji set this out in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why Gandhi chose salt as the issue for civil disobedience in 1930?
o: The salt tax affected all classes and communities, making it a unifying symbol
The British had banned salt consumption
Salt production was controlled by Indian princes
Salt was the largest export of India
questions.x: Salt was a necessity taxed by the state, affecting rich and poor alike.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Subhas Chandra Bose:
1. He was elected Congress president at Haripura (1938) and Tripuri (1939).
2. He resigned the presidency in 1939 after differences with Gandhian leaders.
3. He founded the Indian National Army in 1942.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The INA was first formed by Captain Mohan Singh (1942); Bose revived and led it from 1943.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The RIN mutiny of 1946 alarmed the British government.
Reason (R): It showed that the armed forces could no longer be relied upon to maintain colonial rule.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. August Offer 2. Individual Satyagraha 3. Lahore Resolution of the Muslim League 4. Cripps Mission
questions.x: Lahore Resolution (March 1940), August Offer (August 1940), Individual Satyagraha (October 1940), Cripps (March 1942).

questions.q:
Consider the following legislations of 2025:
1. The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces the Income-tax Act, 1961 from 1 April 2026.
2. The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 prohibits real-money online games.
3. The National Sports Governance Act, 2025 provides for recognition and regulation of national sports bodies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three were enacted in 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following events in West Asia in 2025:
1. Israel and Iran fought a twelve-day conflict in June.
2. The United States struck Iranian nuclear sites, including Fordow.
3. Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three occurred in 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the 'Zero Defect, Zero Effect' (ZED) certification:
1. It is run by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.
2. It encourages quality production with minimum adverse environmental effects.
3. It is mandatory for all MSMEs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
ZED certification is voluntary, with subsidies for participating MSMEs.

questions.q:
After the Pahalgam attack in April 2025, India took which of the following steps?
1. Closed the Attari Integrated Check Post.
2. Cancelled visas issued to Pakistani nationals under the SAARC Visa Exemption Scheme.
3. Expelled all staff of the Pakistan High Commission and closed the mission.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India declared defence advisers persona non grata and cut the High Commission's strength, but did not close it.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the BBNJ Agreement (High Seas Treaty):
1. It deals with marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction.
2. It crossed the number of ratifications needed to enter into force in 2025.
3. It was negotiated under the Convention on Biological Diversity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It is an agreement under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): 'Vande Mataram' became widely known during the Swadeshi movement.
Reason (R): It was part of Bankim Chandra's novel 'Anandamath'.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true; its popularity came from the anti-partition agitation of 1905, not merely from the novel.

questions.q:
Consider the following sporting events and India:
1. Ahmedabad was chosen to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games.
2. India hosted the FIDE Chess World Cup 2025 in Goa.
3. Neeraj Chopra crossed 90 m in javelin for the first time in 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the National Critical Mineral Mission approved in 2025:
1. It covers exploration, overseas acquisition of mineral assets and processing.
2. It includes incentives for recycling critical minerals from scrap and e-waste.
3. Lithium is not classified as a critical mineral in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Lithium is on India's list of critical minerals, along with cobalt, nickel and rare earth elements.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Chandrayaan-3's landing site is called the 'Shiv Shakti point'.
Reason (R): 23 August, the day of the landing, is observed as National Space Day.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true; R is a separate commemoration, not the reason for the name.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A cut in the cash reserve ratio can lower lending rates even if the repo rate is unchanged.
Reason (R): A CRR cut releases lendable resources and reduces the cost of funds for banks.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R correctly explains A.

questions.q:
Which of the following are features of Indian federalism that tilt it towards a strong Centre?
1. Single citizenship
2. All-India Services
3. Appointment of Governors by the Centre
4. Bicameral legislature in every State
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Most States are unicameral; the first three are unitary features.

questions.q:
Consider the following about delimitation:
1. The 84th Amendment froze the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among States until the first Census after 2026.
2. The 2002 delimitation redrew constituency boundaries on the basis of the 2001 Census without changing the number of seats in each State.
3. The Delimitation Commission is a constitutional body under Article 324.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Commission is set up under a Delimitation Act passed by Parliament; Article 324 is about the Election Commission.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Union Budget process:
1. The Annual Financial Statement is laid under Article 112.
2. Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it can be discussed.
3. A Vote on Account is passed under Article 116.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about reservations:
1. Article 16(4A) permits reservation in promotions for SCs and STs.
2. The 50% ceiling on reservations was laid down in Indra Sawhney (1992), subject to exceptional circumstances.
3. EWS reservation under the 103rd Amendment was upheld in Janhit Abhiyan (2022).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the impeachment of the President:
1. The charges may be initiated in either House of Parliament.
2. A 14 days' written notice signed by at least one-fourth of the members of that House is required.
3. Nominated members of Parliament cannot take part in the impeachment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Nominated members, who do not vote in the Presidential election, can take part in impeachment.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Panchayati Raj under the 73rd Amendment:
1. Elections are held every five years and within six months of dissolution.
2. Not less than one-third of seats are reserved for women.
3. The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following languages:
1. Bodo
2. Konkani
3. Maithili
4. Santhali
How many of the above were added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Konkani was added by the 71st Amendment (1992).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the funds of the Union:
1. The Contingency Fund of India is placed at the disposal of the President.
2. Payments from the Public Account of India do not need a parliamentary appropriation.
3. The President's salary is charged on the Contingency Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The President's emoluments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Parliament can alter the boundaries of a State by a simple majority.
Reason (R): Article 4 provides that such laws are not amendments of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: A Bill (not a Money Bill) passed by the Lok Sabha is pending with the Rajya Sabha for more than six months without action. The President may:
o: Summon a joint sitting of both Houses
Refer it to the Supreme Court automatically
questions.x: Correct answer: Summon a joint sitting of both Houses. Article 108 permits a joint sitting when more than six months lapse.

questions.q:
Which of the following are statutory (not constitutional) bodies?
1. National Human Rights Commission
2. Central Vigilance Commission
3. Central Information Commission
4. Comptroller and Auditor General
How many of the above are statutory?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
The CAG is constitutional (Article 148).

questions.q:
Consider the following about linguistic minorities:
1. Article 350A asks States to provide instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage.
2. Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities appointed by the President.
3. The Special Officer reports to the Chief Justice of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Special Officer reports to the President, and reports are laid before Parliament.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Lok Adalats:
1. They work under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
2. Their award is deemed a decree of a civil court.
3. An appeal lies against a Lok Adalat award to the District Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
No appeal lies against a Lok Adalat award.

questions.q: A bank has deposits of ₹1,000 crore. CRR is 3% and SLR 18%. The maximum funds available for lending (ignoring other requirements) are:

Which of the following actions would increase liquidity in the banking system?
1. A cut in the Cash Reserve Ratio
2. Purchase of government securities by the RBI
3. An increase in the repo rate
4. Sale of foreign currency by the RBI in the spot market
How many of the above increase liquidity?
questions.x:
2 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
CRR cut and OMO purchases inject liquidity; a repo hike tightens; selling dollars absorbs rupee liquidity.

questions.q: If the marginal propensity to save is 0.25, an increase in government investment of ₹10,000 crore can raise national income by up to:
questions.x: Multiplier = 1/MPS = 4; 10,000 × 4 = ₹40,000 crore.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about inflation:
1. Core inflation excludes food and fuel.
2. Cost-push inflation can arise from a supply shock such as a rise in crude oil prices.
3. Unanticipated inflation benefits lenders at fixed nominal rates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Unanticipated inflation benefits borrowers, as the real value of debt falls.

questions.q: In a simple banking model, the cash reserve ratio is 20% and banks keep no excess reserves. A fresh deposit of ₹600 crore can lead to a maximum total deposit creation of:
questions.x:
Deposit (money) multiplier = 1 / CRR = 1 / 0.2 = 5.
Total deposits = 600 × 5 = ₹3,000 crore (of which new credit = ₹2,400 crore).

questions.q: A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹1,60,000 and at the end ₹2,62,500. During the year he introduced fresh capital of ₹5,000 and withdrew ₹2,500 for personal use. His profit for the year is:
questions.x:
Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital
= 2,62,500 + 2,500 − 5,000 − 1,60,000 = ₹1,00,000 (statement of affairs method).

questions.q:
Which of the following are fundamental principles of insurance?
1. Utmost good faith
2. Insurable interest
3. Indemnity
4. Speculation
How many of the above are principles of insurance?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Speculation is not a principle; others include proximate cause, subrogation, contribution and mitigation of loss.

questions.q: A machine is purchased for ₹50,000 and ₹3,000 is spent on its installation. Its estimated useful life is 4 years with a residual value of ₹6,000. Annual depreciation under the Straight Line Method is:
questions.x:
SLM depreciation = (Cost + installation − residual value) / useful life.
= (50,000 + 3,000 − 6,000) / 4 = 47,000 / 4 = ₹11,750 per year.
Installation is capitalised as part of cost (AS 10 / Ind AS 16).

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 200 units @ ₹18; 10th — 100 units @ ₹21; 20th — 150 units @ ₹23. 350 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 100 units left come from the latest purchases: 100 × ₹23 = ₹2,300.

questions.q: Rent received in advance ₹4,000 is given as an adjustment. The correct treatment is:
o: Add ₹4,000 to rent received and show it as an asset
Show it only in the balance sheet as an asset
Ignore it until the next year
Deduct ₹4,000 from rent received in the P&L account and show it as a liability in the balance sheet
questions.x: Correct answer: Deduct ₹4,000 from rent received in the P&L account and show it as a liability in the balance sheet. Income received in advance is not earned; it is a current liability.

questions.q:
Consider the following under the Companies Act, 2013:
1. Securities premium can be used to issue fully paid bonus shares.
2. Securities premium can be used to pay dividends.
3. Shares cannot ordinarily be issued at a discount, except sweat equity shares.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
Dividends cannot be paid out of securities premium.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Internal control evaluation helps the auditor decide the extent of test checks.
Reason (R): Strong internal controls reduce the risk of material misstatement going undetected.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Better controls permit smaller samples.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹42,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹3,000; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹1,000; bank charges debited only in the pass book: ₹200; interest credited only in the pass book: ₹300. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹42,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 3,000
− Cheques deposited not credited 1,000
− Bank charges 200
+ Interest credited 300
Pass book balance = ₹44,100.

questions.q: A and B share profits 3:2. C is admitted for a 1/5 share, which he takes equally from A and B. The new ratio is:

The pass book shows an overdraft of ₹12,000. Cheques issued but not presented ₹3,000; cheques deposited but not credited ₹5,000; bank charges ₹200 not in the cash book. The overdraft as per cash book is:
questions.x: Treat the overdraft as a negative balance. Cash book balance = pass-book balance − cheques issued but not presented + cheques deposited but not credited + bank charges not yet entered in the cash book = −12,000 − 3,000 + 5,000 + 200 = −9,800, i.e. an overdraft of ₹9,800.

questions.q: Wages paid for installing new machinery, ₹6,000, were debited to Wages account. If not rectified, the net profit for the year will be:
o: Understated by ₹6,000 less any depreciation that would have been charged on it
questions.x: The capital cost was expensed, reducing profit; had it been capitalised, only depreciation on it would have reduced profit.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Capital introduced by the proprietor is shown on the liabilities side of the balance sheet.
Reason (R): Under the business entity concept, the business is treated as separate from its owner.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Because the entity is separate, it owes the capital to the owner.

questions.q: A worker employed for 4 years and 7 months dies in an accident. Under the gratuity law, gratuity is:
o: Payable to the nominee, as the five-year condition does not apply on death
Payable only if the death is work-related
Not payable, since five years are not completed
questions.x: Correct answer: Payable to the nominee, as the five-year condition does not apply on death. The continuous-service requirement is waived on death or disablement.

questions.q:
Consider the following about standing orders under the IR Code:
1. They apply to industrial establishments with 300 or more workers.
2. An establishment adopting the Central Government's model standing orders is deemed to have certified standing orders.
3. Matters such as classification of workers and misconduct are among the subjects covered.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three reflect Chapter IV of the Code.

questions.q:
With reference to women's employment under the OSH Code, consider the following:
1. Women may work before 6 a.m. and after 7 p.m. with their consent, subject to safety conditions.
2. Women are permitted to work in mines, subject to conditions prescribed for underground work.
3. Women cannot be employed in factories carrying out hazardous processes under any circumstances.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Code allows women in all establishments, including hazardous processes, where adequate safeguards are provided as prescribed.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the need-based minimum wage norms of the 15th Indian Labour Conference (1957):
1. They assume three consumption units per earner's family.
2. They include a net intake of 2,700 calories per average adult.
3. They include 25% for children's education, medical needs and recreation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The 25% component was added by the Supreme Court in Reptakos Brett (1991).

questions.q:
With reference to the Grievance Redressal Committee under the IR Code, consider the following:
1. It is mandatory for every industrial establishment employing twenty or more workers.
2. It has an equal number of members from the employer and the workers, not exceeding ten in total.
3. A worker aggrieved by its decision cannot raise an industrial dispute on the same matter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
A worker dissatisfied with the committee's decision may file an appeal and can then pursue the matter through the conciliation officer, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
How many of the following are Directive Principles that bear directly on labour?
1. Living wage and decent standard of life
2. Participation of workers in management of industries
3. Just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief
4. Protection against traffic in human beings and forced labour
How many of the above are Directive Principles?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
The first three are DPSPs (Articles 43, 43A, 42); protection against forced labour is a Fundamental Right (Article 23).

questions.q:
Match the ILO instrument with its subject:
Instrument:
A. Convention No. 189
B. Convention No. 190
C. Recommendation No. 202
D. Convention No. 144
Subject:
1. Social protection floors
2. Tripartite consultation
3. Violence and harassment in the world of work
4. Domestic workers
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Convention No. 189) → 4 (Domestic workers); B (Convention No. 190) → 3 (Violence and harassment in the world of work); C (Recommendation No. 202) → 1 (Social protection floors); D (Convention No. 144) → 2 (Tripartite consultation).
These are frequently examined ILO instruments.

questions.q:
With reference to the Apprentices Act, 1961, consider the following:
1. Apprentices are trainees and not workers, so labour laws generally do not apply to them.
2. Apprentices receive a stipend.
3. Employers cannot engage apprentices beyond a prescribed band of their workforce.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
The Act prescribes a band (percentage of workforce) for engagement of apprentices.

questions.q:
Consider the following about recognition of negotiating unions under the IR Code:
1. A union with 51% or more of the workers on the muster roll is the sole negotiating union.
2. If no union qualifies, a negotiating council is formed with unions having at least 20% membership.
3. The method of verifying membership is laid down in the Code itself in detail.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Verification is left to rules made by the appropriate government.

questions.q: Arrange in chronological order: 1. Trade Unions Act 2. Industrial Disputes Act 3. Workmen's Compensation Act 4. Payment of Wages Act
questions.x: Workmen's Compensation (1923), Trade Unions (1926), Payment of Wages (1936), Industrial Disputes (1947).

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The OSH Code requires the employer to provide free annual health check-ups to employees of a prescribed age group.
Reason (R): Early detection of occupational disease reduces long-term costs to workers and employers.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Preventive health is the rationale.

questions.q: Which judgment extended maternity benefit to women engaged on muster roll (daily wages) by a municipal body?
o: Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Female Workers (Muster Roll), 2000
questions.x: Correct answer: Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Female Workers (Muster Roll), 2000. The Court relied on Article 42 and CEDAW.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Inspector-cum-Facilitators under the Code on Wages:
1. They may advise employers and workers on compliance.
2. Before prosecuting a first-time contravention, they must give an opportunity to comply within a period.
3. They are appointed by the Supreme Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
They are appointed by the appropriate government.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):
1. It is conducted by the National Statistics Office.
2. Since 2025 it also provides monthly estimates of key indicators in Current Weekly Status.
3. It uses Current Daily Status as its only measure of activity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
PLFS reports usual status and Current Weekly Status estimates.

questions.q: A firm handles employee complaints in three stages — supervisor, head of department, then a joint grievance committee — before voluntary arbitration. This follows:
o: The Model Grievance Procedure evolved under the Code of Discipline
questions.x: The Model Grievance Procedure provides graded steps ending in voluntary arbitration.

questions.q: An EPF member in continuous service dies. Average monthly wages over the last 12 months were ₹9,500 and the average balance in the member's PF account over that period was ₹1,70,000. The assurance benefit under the EDLI Scheme is:
questions.x:
EDLI = 35 × average monthly wages (ceiling ₹15,000) + 50% of the average PF balance (bonus capped at ₹1,75,000), subject to a minimum of ₹2.5 lakh and a maximum of ₹7 lakh.
35 × 9,500 = ₹3,32,500; bonus = min(50% × 1,70,000, 1,75,000) = ₹85,000.
Total ₹4,17,500.

questions.q:
With reference to SPREE 2025 of ESIC, consider the following:
1. It encouraged voluntary registration of unregistered employers and employees.
2. Registered employers would not face inspection or demand for periods prior to registration, subject to the scheme's terms.
3. It made ESI coverage voluntary for all establishments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Coverage remains mandatory where the Act applies; SPREE was a one-time registration drive.

questions.q: An employee draws basic wages plus DA of ₹19,000 per month and both employer and employee contribute 12% on actual wages. How much of the employer's share goes to the EPF (provident fund) account each month?
questions.x:
Employer's 12% of 19,000 = ₹2,280.
EPS share is capped at 8.33% of ₹15,000 = ₹1,250.
EPF share = 2,280 − 1,250 = ₹1,030.

questions.q:
Match the scheme with the correct feature:
Scheme:
A. Unified Pension Scheme
B. National Pension System
C. Atal Pension Yojana
D. PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan
Feature:
1. Defined contribution with market-linked returns
2. Assured 50% of average basic pay after 25 years
3. Guaranteed ₹1,000–5,000 pension, entry age 18–40
4. ₹3,000 pension with matching government contribution
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Unified Pension Scheme) → 2 (Assured 50% of average basic pay after 25 years); B (National Pension System) → 1 (Defined contribution with market-linked returns); C (Atal Pension Yojana) → 3 (Guaranteed ₹1,000–5,000 pension, entry age 18–40); D (PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan) → 4 (₹3,000 pension with matching government contribution).
Each scheme's defining feature.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Contributory schemes such as EPF are classed as social insurance.
Reason (R): In social insurance, benefits depend on contributions made during working life.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Social assistance, by contrast, is financed from general taxes and paid on need.

questions.q: Under the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995, a member retires at 58 with pensionable salary of ₹14,500 and pensionable service of 22 years (including any weightage). The monthly member pension is:
questions.x:
Monthly pension = (Pensionable salary × Pensionable service) / 70
= (14,500 × 22) / 70 = ₹4,557.
Pensionable salary is the average of the last 60 months' wages (subject to the ₹15,000 ceiling), and the minimum pension is ₹1,000.

questions.q:
Consider the following about cash benefits under the ESI scheme:
1. Sickness benefit is paid at 70% of average daily wages for up to 91 days in a year.
2. Maternity benefit is paid at 100% of average daily wages.
3. Dependants' benefit is paid only as a one-time lump sum.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Dependants' benefit is a monthly payment, shared among dependants at 90% of wages.

questions.q:
Match the scheme with its cover:
Scheme:
A. PMJJBY
B. PMSBY
C. PM-JAY
D. PMJDY RuPay card (after Aug 2018)
Cover:
1. ₹2 lakh accident insurance
2. ₹5 lakh per family per year for hospitalisation
3. ₹2 lakh on death due to any cause
4. ₹2 lakh on accidental death or total disability
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (PMJJBY) → 3 (₹2 lakh on death due to any cause); B (PMSBY) → 4 (₹2 lakh on accidental death or total disability); C (PM-JAY) → 2 (₹5 lakh per family per year for hospitalisation); D (PMJDY RuPay card (after Aug 2018)) → 1 (₹2 lakh accident insurance).
Note that PMSBY covers only accidents while PMJJBY covers death from any cause.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Methane is a major target for short-term climate action.
Reason (R): Methane traps far more heat per tonne than CO₂ but stays in the atmosphere for only about a decade.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Cutting it gives fast results.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Lakes in cold regions freeze from the top, so aquatic life survives below.
Reason (R): Water is densest at about 4 °C, and ice is less dense than liquid water.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Ice floats and insulates the water beneath.

questions.q: An employee receives an e-mail that looks like it is from the bank, asking them to 'verify' their account by clicking a link. What is the safest response?
o: Reply to the e-mail asking if it is genuine
Do not click; contact the bank through its official website or number
Forward it to colleagues to check
Click the link but enter only the user name
questions.x: Verify through an independent official channel; replies go to the attacker.

questions.q:
Consider the following about domestic fuels:
1. LPG is mainly a mixture of propane and butane.
2. A strong-smelling compound such as ethyl mercaptan is added to LPG to help detect leaks.
3. CNG is mainly propane.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
CNG is mainly methane.

questions.q:
Consider the following about nuclear fusion:
1. It joins light nuclei such as hydrogen isotopes.
2. It powers the Sun and other stars.
3. Commercial fusion power plants are already in operation in several countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Fusion remains experimental, e.g., ITER in France, of which India is a member.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): GPUs are widely used to train artificial intelligence models.
Reason (R): A GPU has thousands of simpler cores that perform many calculations in parallel, suited to matrix operations.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Neural-network training is dominated by large matrix multiplications.

questions.q:
Match the keyboard shortcut with its common action in office software:
Shortcut:
A. Ctrl + Z
B. Ctrl + Y
C. Ctrl + P
D. Ctrl + F
Action:
1. Undo
2. Print
3. Redo
4. Find
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Ctrl + Z) → 1 (Undo); B (Ctrl + Y) → 3 (Redo); C (Ctrl + P) → 2 (Print); D (Ctrl + F) → 4 (Find).
Standard shortcuts in most office applications.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker.
Reason (R): Raising the pressure above the liquid raises the boiling point of water.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Water boils at around 120 °C inside, so heat transfer is faster.

questions.q:
Match the network device with its main function:
Device:
A. Router
B. Switch
C. Modem
D. Firewall
Function:
1. Forwards packets between different networks
2. Filters traffic according to security rules
3. Converts digital signals for transmission over a line and back
4. Connects devices within a local network using MAC addresses
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Router) → 1 (Forwards packets between different networks); B (Switch) → 4 (Connects devices within a local network using MAC addresses); C (Modem) → 3 (Converts digital signals for transmission over a line and back); D (Firewall) → 2 (Filters traffic according to security rules).
Each device works at a different layer of networking.

questions.q:
Consider the following about tropical cyclones:
1. They do not form within about 5° of the equator.
2. In the Northern Hemisphere they rotate anticlockwise.
3. They gain strength as they move over land.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Near the equator the Coriolis force is too weak; over land they lose their moisture supply and weaken.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Fish-eating birds often have higher DDT levels than the fish they eat.
Reason (R): Persistent chemicals accumulate in fatty tissue and become more concentrated at each step of the food chain.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. This is biomagnification.

questions.q:
Match the vaccine with its type:
Vaccine:
A. Oral polio vaccine
B. Injectable polio vaccine (IPV)
C. Tetanus vaccine
D. Hepatitis B vaccine
Type:
1. Inactivated
2. Live attenuated
3. Toxoid
4. Recombinant subunit
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Oral polio vaccine) → 2 (Live attenuated); B (Injectable polio vaccine (IPV)) → 1 (Inactivated); C (Tetanus vaccine) → 3 (Toxoid); D (Hepatitis B vaccine) → 4 (Recombinant subunit).
Vaccine types differ in what they present to the immune system.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Antibiotics are not useful against the common cold.
Reason (R): The common cold is caused by viruses, which antibiotics do not kill.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Misuse of antibiotics also drives antimicrobial resistance.

questions.q:
Consider the following about antimicrobial resistance (AMR):
1. Misuse and overuse of antibiotics speed up the development of resistance.
2. Resistant bacteria can spread between humans, animals and the environment.
3. AMR is a problem only in hospitals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Community spread and farm use of antibiotics also matter; this is the 'One Health' view.

questions.q: At what time between 7 and 8 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
questions.x:
At 7:00 the minute hand is 35 minute-spaces behind the hour hand.
To coincide it must gain 35 spaces; it gains 55 spaces in 60 minutes.
Time = 35 × 60/55 = 420/11 minutes = 38 2/11 minutes past 7.

questions.q: A motor boat goes 80 km downstream in 5 hours and returns the same distance upstream in 8 hours. The speed of the stream is:
questions.x:
Downstream speed = 80/5 = 16 km/h; upstream speed = 80/8 = 10 km/h.
Stream = (down − up)/2 = (16 − 10)/2 = 3 km/h (boat in still water = 13 km/h).

questions.q: A, B and C can complete a contract alone in 25, 30 and 27 days respectively. Working together they finish it and receive ₹74,500. If payment is in proportion to the work done, C's share is:
questions.x:
Daily work rates are 1/25 : 1/30 : 1/27 = 54 : 45 : 50 (LCM 1350).
Working together, work done is in the same ratio, so C gets 50/149 × 74,500 = ₹25,000.

questions.q: In a row, Deepak is 14th from the left and Rekha is 17th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Deepak becomes 24th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Deepak occupies Rekha's old place, which is 17th from the right and now 24th from the left.
Total = 24 + 17 − 1 = 40.

questions.q: Given log₁₀ 2 = 0.3010 and log₁₀ 3 = 0.4771, how many digits are there in 6^58?
questions.x:
log₁₀(6^58) = 58 × log₁₀ 6 = 58 × 0.7781 = 45.1298.
The characteristic is 45, so the number of digits = 45 + 1 = 46.

questions.q: Find the remainder when 2^180 is divided by 7.
questions.x:
Powers of 2 mod 7: 2, 4, 1 → cycle length 3.
180 = 3 × 60 + 0 → 2^180 ≡ 2^3 ≡ 1 (mod 7).

questions.q: Find the greatest number that will divide 102, 210, 282 leaving the same remainder in each case.
questions.x:
If N leaves the same remainder, N divides the differences.
Differences: 210 − 102 = 108, 282 − 210 = 72.
HCF(108, 72) = 36.

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 4, 5, 12, 39, 160, ?
Find the next term in the series: E3H, I7L, M15P, Q27T, ?
questions.x:
First letters advance by 4 (E, I, M, Q, U); the last letter is always 3 places after the first; the numbers increase by 4, 8, 12, … (3, 7, 15, 27, 43).
Next term: U43X.

questions.q: The daily output of a cement plant rises by 10%, then falls by 25%, and finally rises by 20%. The overall percentage change is:
questions.x:
Multiply the growth factors: (1 + 10/100) × (1 − 25/100) × (1 + 20/100) = 1.1 × 0.75 × 1.2 = 0.99.
Overall change = (0.99 − 1) × 100 = -1% → 1% decrease.
Note: simply adding (10 − 25 + 20) is wrong because each change acts on a new base.

questions.q: The average of 11 observations is 45. The average of the first 6 is 50 and that of the last 6 is 58. The 6th observation is:
questions.x:
Sum of all 11 = 11 × 45 = 495.
First 6 + last 6 = 6×50 + 6×58 = 648; the middle observation is counted twice.
Middle = 648 − 495 = 153.

questions.q: How many arrangements of the letters of 'PREMIUM' are there in which the vowels are NOT all together?
questions.x:
Total arrangements = 2,520 (M appears 2 times).
Vowels together = 60 × 6 = 360.
Not all together = 2,520 − 360 = 2,160.

questions.q: In a certain code, 'A $ B' means A is the sister of B; 'A @ B' means A is the husband of B; 'A × B' means A is the mother of B; 'A + B' means A is the father of B. If 'K + P × R' (read as K + P and P × R), how is K related to R?
questions.x:
K + P: K is the father of P. P × R: P is the mother of R.
Combining the two (all persons taken to be of one family, as is conventional): K is the maternal grandfather of R.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 6 : 5. After 4 years, the ratio will become 46 : 39. What is P's present age?
The monthly incomes of P and Q are in the ratio 9 : 7 and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 5 : 3. If each of them saves ₹20,000 a month, P's monthly income is:
questions.x:
Let incomes = 9k, 7k and expenditures = 5m, 3m.
9k − 5m = 7k − 3m = 20,000 → 2k = 2m.
Solving gives k = 5,000, m = 5,000.
P's income = 9 × 5,000 = ₹45,000 (check: ₹45,000 − ₹25,000 = ₹20,000).
